assumptions: OpenTsiolkovsky 1.0.0 (MIT, external binary -- not vendored; see NOTICE; openTsiolkovsky-v1.0.0-<platform>.tar.gz, pinned per-platform SHA-256 digests live in scripts/fetch_opentsiolkovsky.py)
OT pos_eci_*/vel_eci_* read as LAUNCH_ECI (axes = ECEF at the launch epoch, held inertial) and converted to GCRS by orbitopt.flightlab.frames.to_gcrs at the epoch
created_utc is the mission epoch: this adapter is a pure function of (target, vehicle, attitude program), so repeated calls write byte-identical runs
vehicle: Block 1 figures throughout (booster 71 m / 275 t dry / 3,250 t propellant; ship 50.3 m / ~100 t dry / ~1,200 t propellant) so the stack is one consistent generation; later blocks differ.

vehicle: Raptor 2 is taken at 2.256 MN sea-level thrust and 327 s sea-level Isp (published) with a vacuum Isp of 350 s; sources disagree on the Raptor 2 vacuum figure (350 vs 363 s) and the Raptor Vacuum is 380 s. The ship's 3 sea-level + 3 vacuum engines are carried as one engine at the thrust-weighted effective vacuum Isp (365 s); its 14.76 MN total matches the published ~14.7 MN.

vehicle: The booster's 33-engine set is modelled at the 95 % figure with an illustrative throttle schedule (full to 100 s, then down to hold the 3.0 g target limit, within the published 40-100 % Raptor throttle band) and cuts off at 135 s; the unburned propellant at cutoff is the boostback and landing budget.
vehicle: Hot staging is modelled as ship ignition at the separation instant; the real ship lights its engines before the stages part.

vehicle: The booster section models its 13 relightable engines as one set with a 40 % throttle floor; the real vehicle shuts down to 3 engines for the last seconds of the landing burn, which one engine set cannot express.
vehicle: Nose length is not published, so the tangent ogive is declared 1.5 diameters long (illustrative, +-30 %). Blunting of the real tip, the flaps and the grid fins are not in the generated aero.

target: Constraint basis (E5-07): every limit above is PUBLIC SOURCE or ASSUMPTION as commented; none was widened to make the computed flight close. Vehicle-parameter uncertainty (generated aero +-30 %, nose length +-30 % assumption) is recorded as the SENSITIVITY RANGE of the reference, quantified in the E5-07 sensitivity record (scripts/e507_reference.py sensitivity), not by loosening a limit.

target: q*alpha structural load (a Starship-class sizing case the E5-05 fixture never carried): the reference does not impose an unpublished allowable as a number. It is qualified as a REPORTED load -- the ascent run carries q and the attitude program's angle of attack (gravity-turn: beta ~ 0, q*alpha ~ 0 by construction of the commanded program), and the sensitivity record evaluates the +-30 % aerodynamic band on the same trajectory. The entry cross-check is reported separately as not-closable with the current guidance chain (see the E5-07 report).

target: Thrust-to-weight ratio: liftoff TWR of the declared stack is 74.93 MN vacuum thrust (33 x Raptor 2 at 95 %, derived from the published 2.256 MN sea-level figure) on 3,525 t at pad -> 2.17 vacuum / ~1.95 sea-level-class; the published Block 1 liftoff TWR is ~1.5. The OT backend flies the declared full-thrust burn window (no throttle authority), so the declared thrust curve -- not a mission gate -- carries this figure; it is reported in the E5-07 record as a vehicle-capability note.

target: The vehicle flies its DECLARED attitude program and burn windows (fixed-program OT flight; the program in the vehicle file is an authored gravity-turn-style profile, scenario choice, tagged illustrative there).

target: Booster RTLS: the vehicle models two relightable ignitions (boostback, landing) and AERODYNAMIC entry (no entry burn). The E3 recovery chain as shipped plans a powered entry script (1 + entry_burns ignitions); the E5-07 record reports the booster-recovery leg's closability against that capability honestly -- see docs/physics-qualification.md.
